status_summary: ODNI announced a restructuring called ODNI 2.0 on 2025-08-20, targeting a size reduction of more than 40 percent by the end of FY2025 and savings above $700 million a year; contemporaneous reports put staffing near 1,500, down from just under 2,000 in January 2025, and described three mission centers as refocused with functions moved to the Mission Integration office and the National Intelligence Council (Defense One). Title LXIV of Public Law 119-60 (signed 2025-12-18) repealed the DNI's authority to establish new national intelligence centers, required the DNI to submit a staffing end-state and plan within 120 days, required termination of the National Counterproliferation and Biosecurity Center within 180 days and wound down the Office of Engagement, without setting a numerical staff cap. After DNI Gabbard left in June 2026, acting DNI Bill Pulte announced further rounds of layoffs, which he described in late July as a near-final round of about 30 percent, and the Senate confirmed Jay Clayton as DNI on 2026-07-28 by 51-47 (Roll Call). No amendment to Executive Order 12333 giving the DNI stronger budget and personnel authority was found.

timeline.event: ODNI announces ODNI 2.0: a reduction of more than 40 percent in office size by the end of FY2025 and more than $700 million in annual savings, with redundant missions, functions and personnel to be eliminated.

Trade press reports that the Foreign Malign Influence Center, National Counterproliferation and Biosecurity Center and Cyber Threat Intelligence Integration Center are being refocused with core functions folded into Mission Integration and the National Intelligence Council, that the External Research Council and Strategic Futures Group are being terminated, and that staff fell from just under 2,000 to about 1,500.

Public Law 119-60 (FY2026 NDAA) is signed. Its intelligence division (Title LXIV) repeals the DNI's authority to create new national intelligence centers (Sec. 6402), requires a staffing end-state and plan within 120 days (Sec. 6403), requires termination of the National Counterproliferation and Biosecurity Center within 180 days (Sec. 6404), and winds down the Office of Engagement effective 90 days after enactment (Sec. 6405); it sets no numerical ODNI staff cap.

DNI Tulsi Gabbard leaves office (she announced her resignation in May 2026, citing a family medical matter, per Hawaii News Now). Bill Pulte, who also directs the Federal Housing Finance Agency, becomes acting DNI and is directed to begin downsizing ODNI (per ASA Online).

Acting DNI Pulte announces a fourth round of ODNI layoffs (exact day in July 2026 not confirmed). The Washington Post, as relayed by Federal News Network, reports about 200 employees laid off or reassigned since June 1 and an ODNI a little over half its January 2025 size of about 2,000.

Senate confirms Jay Clayton as DNI, 51-47. Roll Call reports Pulte described a fifth and near-final round of terminations amounting to roughly a 30 percent staff reduction; Democrats had objected to an unconfirmed acting official carrying out the cuts.

NBC News, as relayed by an ABC affiliate, reported that the fifth round of ODNI terminations announced by acting DNI Pulte could leave ODNI with about 1,000 employees, down from about 2,000 at the start of 2025; the relayed report mentions no legal challenge.

title: Downsize ODNI and refocus it on directing rather than duplicating IC functions
uncertainties: Staff counts differ by source: the ODNI release gives percentages but no headcount, the Washington Post figures come second-hand via Federal News Network, and a Wikipedia summary of Gabbard's tenure says staff was cut by 50 percent. The Federal News Network article is dated July 2026 without a day. A Wikipedia summary reports that the National Intelligence Council was moved into the DNI's office in May 2025 and two officials were fired; not confirmed from a primary source. Title LXIV of Public Law 119-60 was read on the Senate intelligence committee's copy and contains no ODNI staff cap; the earlier Senate proposal to transfer the National Counterintelligence and Security Center to the FBI was not in that title, and the last part of the committee copy was not read. Whether the DNI submitted the required staffing end-state report and whether the counterproliferation center was terminated on schedule were not verified. The 2026 layoffs and the DNI confirmation rest on news reports, not on ODNI or Senate pages. Clayton's sworn-in date (2026-08-03) was seen only in an ODNI newsroom listing.
